title: Affinity-based Optimizations for TFHE on Processing-in-DRAM
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption over the Torus (TFHE) is a compute- and bandwidth-intensive workload; when mapped to Processing-in-Memory (PIM/HBM) architectures, existing accelerators over-exploit parallelism at the expense of data affinity, causing excessive remote data accesses (RDAs) that degrade performance due to PIM's limited inter-bank communication bandwidth.
motivation: PIM architectures offer high internal bandwidth that can dramatically accelerate TFHE, but the workload's affinity patterns must be respected to avoid the remote-access bottleneck that nullifies bandwidth advantages.
method: The paper applies algorithmic optimizations to TFHE to restructure its sub-tasks (bootstrapping, key-switching, NTT/FFT operations) so that data accessed together is co-located on the same PIM vault or bank. An offline scheduler analyzes the affinity patterns of TFHE sub-tasks—determining which operands are used together and how frequently—and derives an optimal scheduling order that minimizes RDAs while maintaining sufficient parallelism. The approach is validated on a variant of an existing PIM-HBM device with minimal hardware modifications and evaluated on a real FPGA-based PIM system emulator.
key_novelty: An affinity-pattern-driven offline scheduling framework for TFHE on PIM that minimizes remote data accesses by co-scheduling operations with shared data onto the same PIM units.
contributions: Analysis of data affinity patterns in TFHE sub-tasks (bootstrapping, key-switching, NTT) on PIM architectures.
An offline affinity-aware scheduler that minimizes RDAs while maintaining parallelism.
Algorithmic restructuring of TFHE to expose better data locality on PIM.
4.24x to 209x speedup over prior TFHE accelerators on real-world benchmarks on a FPGA-based PIM system.

metrics.speedup: 4.24x to 209x over prior TFHE accelerators on real-world benchmarks

limitations: Results are from an FPGA-based PIM emulator rather than a fabricated PIM ASIC, so absolute performance numbers may not transfer directly to production hardware.
primary_theme: Affinity-aware scheduling of TFHE on processing-in-DRAM to minimize remote accesses
